requirements.description: Fellowships are provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility. Excellence of the researcher is an explicit framing criterion for the fellowship instrument.

European Postdoctoral Fellowships must take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and are open to researchers of any nationality wishing to come to Europe or move within Europe. Standard duration: 12–24 months.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships must involve an outgoing phase (12–24 months) at an organisation in a non-associated Third Country, followed by a mandatory 12-month return phase to a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Open to European nationals or long-term residents only.

Researchers receiving a Postdoctoral Fellowship may include a secondment phase within the overall fellowship duration. For European Fellowships, secondment cannot exceed half the requested duration (excluding non-academic placement period). For Global Fellowships, secondment is permitted for up to half the outgoing phase (max 3 months at start at beneficiary). No secondments during the mandatory return period.

An additional period of up to six months for a non-academic sector placement may be included at the end of the project, at an organisation established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. The request must be integral to the proposal and must explain added value for the project and researcher career development.
requirements.source_section: Scope – Placements in the non-academic sector

requirements.description: Training activities must integrate key transferable skills and competences including digital skills (e.g. generative AI), foster Open Science culture, knowledge valorisation, research integrity, and where applicable innovation and entrepreneurship. Fellows must be prepared for digital collaboration, FAIR data management, and societal engagement.

A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, covering research objectives, training and career needs, transferable skills, teaching, publications, and participation in open science events. The Plan must be submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action and can be updated when needed.

Organisations active in nuclear research in EU Member States or Euratom-associated countries are eligible for MSCA PF fellowships in Euratom research areas. Specific eligibility conditions apply as described in Annex B.
ERA Fellowships implemented through Work Programme Annex 11 provide specific support for researchers undertaking fellowships in widening countries, supporting balanced brain circulation.
